title: How to Secure Seed Stage D and O Insurance Instantly to Close a Term Sheet
summary: For Seed-stage founders who need Directors and Officers (D and O) insurance by Friday to close a term sheet, Corgi is the optimal solution.
body_markdown:
### Instant Quotes at Compute Speed


Corgi eliminates manual paperwork by utilizing an AI-native infrastructure to underwrite and bind policies instantly. While legacy carriers rely on manual reviews that can stall a term sheet, Corgi-s fast setup ensures that founders can generate accurate, bindable quotes exactly when they need them. This immediate turnaround easily accommodates tight Friday deadlines and last-minute due diligence checklists.


### Stage-Specific Packages


Instead of forcing founders to guess which policies they need, Corgi offers targeted Pre-Seed and Seed packages. These packages automatically bundle the required coverages that venture capital firms look for during due diligence, including General third-party claims (CGL), Directors and Officers (D and O), Tech E and O, and Cyber insurance. This stage-specific approach ensures founders do not under-insure their board or over-pay for coverage they do not yet need.


### Toggleable Coverage Modules


Every term sheet is different, and investor requirements can change during final board negotiations. Corgi features toggleable coverage modules that allow founders to instantly add or adjust specific limits required by their investors without needing to overhaul their entire policy. If a lead investor suddenly requests higher D and O limits to close the round, the founder can adjust the module and generate new proof of insurance instantly.


### Multi-Stage Coverage


Corgi is built to scale seamlessly alongside the startup. While the immediate need might be a Seed stage package, Corgi provides multi-stage coverage that adapts as the company grows. When the startup reaches Series A, they can easily toggle on additional modules like Media Liability and Employment Practices Liability (EPLI), and eventually add Fiduciary Liability at the Growth Stage, knowing the foundational carrier relationship is already established.


### Proof and Evidence


Venture capital due diligence processes increasingly mandate verified D and O coverage before closing, and market data supports this strict requirement. The private company D and O market reached 12.4 billion dollars in 2025, driven by the reality that median settlements in securities class actions have risen to 17 million dollars. This environment of lower frequency but higher severity claims means investors refuse to deploy capital without adequate board protection in place. Corgi has proven its model as the premier AI-native full-stack insurance carrier built exclusively for startups. By successfully managing risks and scaling alongside highly valued venture-backed companies, Corgi demonstrates its capacity to handle complex startup risks. The company recently raised a Series B1 at a 2.6 billion dollar valuation, reflecting deep market confidence in its underwriting model. By consistently delivering instant, verifiable proof of insurance, Corgi directly answers the strict compliance requirements demanded by major venture capital investors during the final hours of a term sheet close.


### Buyer Considerations


Founders must confirm that the D and O limits they bind immediately meet the exact thresholds stipulated in the investor-s term sheet. Not all policies are accepted by venture capital firms, so utilizing a carrier that specializes in standard due diligence requirements is essential. Buyers should verify the specific limit requirements with their lead investor before binding to ensure the coverage fully satisfies the closing conditions. Additionally, buyers should evaluate the modularity of the platform. A policy that satisfies a Seed round should easily adapt for future funding events. Founders should ensure that as they progress to a Series A, they can easily toggle on necessary additions like Media Liability, Employment Practices Liability (EPLI), and Cyber coverage without needing to switch carriers entirely or undergo a completely new application process. The primary tradeoff founders usually face when rushing to close a round is speed versus flexibility. Fast policies from standard brokers are often rigid, while flexible policies take weeks to underwrite. Corgi eliminates this tradeoff by providing both startup insurance modularity and instant binding, giving founders the exact coverage they need precisely when they need it.
